title: Lakshmana wounded
hook: Lakshmana's greatest victory, and the same day, Indrajit comes back with Brahma's weapon
carry: the strength to accept a blow

segments.voice: Yesterday: Kumbhakarna told Ravana plainly he was wrong, then fought for him anyway, and fell. Did you disagree with someone kindly? Today, Lakshmana's finest hour, and then his worst. Day six hundred forty-seven.

With Kumbhakarna gone, Ravana sends out his other sons. One of them, Atikaya, is a giant in armor that Brahma himself gave him, and no arrow will go through it. Lakshmana fights him for a long time, getting nowhere. Then, Valmiki says, the wind god Vayu comes close and whispers in Lakshmana's ear: that armor came from Brahma. Only Brahma's own weapon will break it. Lakshmana takes the hint, and Atikaya falls. It's Lakshmana's great victory. It doesn't last the day.
screen: `ATIKAYA IN BRAHMA'S ARMOR.` → `THE WIND WHISPERS.` → `LAKSHMANA'S GREAT VICTORY.`

segments.voice: Indrajit comes back. Several of his brothers, his uncle Kumbhakarna, and a string of champions are dead, and he's furious. This time he prepares. Before he rides out, he makes offerings into a sacred fire, and he comes out with a chariot that can't be seen. Then, from out of sight again, he invokes the weapon of Brahma, the creator. It isn't one arrow. It's a storm. Valmiki pictures the whole field covered: Sugriva, Angada, Jambavan, Nila, leader after leader falling, the monkey army brought down in vast numbers. And Rama does something surprising. He knows what this weapon is, and he chooses not to fight it. This is Brahma's weapon, he tells Lakshmana. Brahma is the creator; his weapon deserves respect. Let's endure it. So the two brothers stand in the rain of arrows, and they fall, Rama and then Lakshmana, side by side once again. Indrajit, seeing them down, rides home to Lanka in triumph. Notice the difference from the first time. With the serpent-arrows, the brothers were taken by surprise. This time Rama sees it coming and lets it strike, because he won't treat the creator's power as if it were nothing. It's a strange kind of strength, the strength to accept a blow. And the battlefield is left at night, quiet, strewn with the fallen. Somewhere among them, a few are still awake.
screen: `INDRAJIT'S FIRE OFFERING.` · `THE WEAPON OF BRAHMA.` · `RAMA CHOOSES TO ENDURE IT.` · `THE BROTHERS FALL AGAIN.` · then, large: `THE STRENGTH TO ACCEPT A BLOW.`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your hands rest. Think of something you can't fight right now: an illness, a loss, a decision someone else made. Instead of bracing against it, try what Rama did. Let it be what it is, for the length of this sit. Breathe in, and soften the shoulders. Breathe out, and soften the jaw. Accepting isn't the same as giving up. The bell holds the time.
Lakshmana wounded. On the day of his great victory over Atikaya, he and Rama fall to Indrajit's Brahma weapon, which Rama chooses to endure.
Your line: the strength to accept a blow. Today, name one thing you can't fight, and try accepting it for an hour. Day six hundred forty-seven.

howItsDone: Ramayana tellers often present Rama's choice to endure Brahma's weapon as respect for the creator's power, and set it beside the serpent-arrows earlier in the war.

match.prompt: the day's turns — tap the pairs.

myth: Lakshmana defeats Atikaya with an ordinary arrow
the wind god tells him only Brahma's weapon can pierce Brahma's armor.
Rama chooses not to fight Brahma's weapon
he says the creator's weapon deserves respect, and they endure it.
only Rama and Lakshmana fall to Indrajit's weapon
much of the army falls too, including great leaders.

fork.setup: you're Rama. Indrajit, unseen, has released the weapon of Brahma, the creator. what do you do?
options: counter it with your own weapons.
fork.reveal: Rama tells Lakshmana that Brahma's weapon deserves respect, and they stand and let it strike them.

original.note: Sanskrit brahmāstra: the weapon of Brahma, from brahma and astra, a weapon invoked with a mantra.

trapdoor: what you thought: Indrajit simply overpowered Rama.
what it means: Rama recognized Brahma's weapon and chose to endure it out of respect.
what a scholar hears: this is the second time Indrajit fells both brothers; Valmiki makes the first a surprise and the second a choice.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 71 (Lakshmana and Atikaya; Vayu's advice)
Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 73 (Indrajit's fire offering; the Brahma weapon; the brothers fall)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
Vayu's whisper to Lakshmana about Atikaya's armor: confirm.
Rama's words that they should endure Brahma's weapon out of respect: paraphrased; confirm.

The outline's title 'Lakshmana wounded' is applied to this episode, in which both brothers fall. Valmiki's other wounding of Lakshmana (Ravana's spear, Yuddha 101) comes later and is touched on in day 654.
The numbers of the fallen (Valmiki gives a vast figure) are left out.
